strengths: Well-motivated spectral analysis of VAE latents (Section 3) provides clear intuition for scale-wise generation; RAPSD plots for SDXL and SD3.5 effectively demonstrate that noise masks high frequencies at high noise levels

Comprehensive experimental validation including multiple automated metrics (FID, CLIP, ImageReward, PickScore, GenEval), professional human preference studies across multiple criteria (128 PartiPrompts), ablation studies on all design choices, and testing on multiple model sizes (SD3.5 M/L)
Substantial practical speedups (2.5-10×) demonstrated with human evaluation showing clear preference over most baselines, particularly in image complexity and aesthetics

Solid technical execution with well-justified design choices: Table 1 validates upscaling x₀ before noise injection vs alternatives, ablations validate time schedule shifting, synthetic data importance, and PDM loss contributions
Clear presentation with informative figures, reproducible implementation details, and extensive supplementary materials with additional qualitative comparisons
weaknesses: Limited core novelty: scale-wise/progressive generation is established (VAEs, GANs, cascaded DMs, next-scale prediction); spectral analysis builds on prior work (Dieleman 2024, Rissanen et al.); main contribution is engineering application of these existing ideas to distillation

Inconsistent automated metric results undermine claims: Table 4 shows SWD-M FID of 23.0 (COCO) vs DMD2-SDXL at 14.3; PickScore improvements marginal (0.230 vs 0.231); CLIP scores nearly identical across methods (~0.355), reducing confidence in quality claims

Heavy reliance on synthetic training data: Table 5D shows dramatic performance degradation with real data (FID: 28.7 vs 13.6); raises concerns about practical applicability, generalization, and fairness of comparisons to other methods

Manual scale schedule design lacks principled approach: schedules appear hand-crafted (256→384→512→640→768→1024); no analysis of sensitivity to schedule choices; adaptive scheduling deferred to future work limits practical applicability

Limited scope of applicability: only evaluated on text-to-image with transformer-based latent DMs; unclear generalization to video, 3D, or other tasks; method heavily dependent on teacher quality at low resolutions (Fig. 4 shows SDXL fails at 256×256)

Statistical rigor concerns: no error bars or confidence intervals; human evaluation on only 128 prompts; no significance testing or multiple seeds reported; makes it difficult to assess reliability of improvements
Missing key comparisons with cascaded DMs despite acknowledging them as related work; cascaded DMs also perform multi-stage generation but not directly compared, limiting validation of uniqueness

PDM loss analysis incomplete: Table 6 shows enormous gap vs naive patch loss but this validates averaging strategy rather than MMD formulation; Table 5G shows linear vs RBF kernels perform identically, questioning whether MMD kernel choice matters
Presentation overclaiming: states method 'surpasses full-resolution distilled models' but Table 2 shows worse FID for 4-6 step SWD configurations; framing needs more care given metric inconsistencies

strengths: Clear spectral analysis motivation: Well-presented analysis (Section 3, Figure 1) showing that VAE latents follow power-law distributions and noise masks high frequencies at high noise levels, providing solid intuition for scale-wise operation

Practical and elegant method: Simple modification to existing distillation pipelines (DMD2) with clear engineering choices (upsampling strategy validated in Table 1, time schedule shifting, synthetic data training)

Comprehensive experimental evaluation: Multiple models (SD3.5 M/L), multiple metrics (FID, CLIP, IR, PickScore, GenEval), human preference study with professional assessors, and thorough ablations (Tables 5, 7) validating all major design choices
Strong empirical speedups: Achieves 2-10× speedup with competitive quality; shows ~2× speedup at same step count with minimal degradation, and superior results under equivalent time constraints
Novel Patch Distribution Matching (PDM): Useful contribution requiring no additional models; can serve as standalone distillation objective; comparison to naive patch loss (Table 6) justifies design
Good reproducibility: Detailed implementation details (learning rates, batch sizes, iteration counts, GPU setup) in appendices facilitate reproduction
weaknesses: Limited conceptual novelty: Progressive resolution generation is well-established in VAEs, GANs, cascaded diffusion, and next-scale prediction. The contribution is primarily application to distillation—useful but incremental rather than conceptually novel

Spectral analysis limited in scope: Motivation specific to VAE-based latent diffusion; doesn't apply to pixel-space diffusion or other architectures, limiting theoretical generalizability and guidance for future model families

Teacher model dependency unclear: SD3.5 generates cropped images at 256×256 yet distillation succeeds; SDXL generates no plausible images yet method works. Questions whether approach exploits distillation to fix teacher limitations versus robustly handling poor conditions

Quality trade-offs not fully resolved: Table 2 shows FID sometimes worse for scale-wise (e.g., 23.0 vs 20.4 at 6 steps). Automated metrics and human evaluation sometimes disagree, suggesting real quality loss in some configurations

Scale schedule design underexplored: Choice of 256×256 starting resolution justified only by 'marginal speed improvements'; no systematic study of schedule sensitivity; no design principles for practitioners on new models; schedules appear somewhat arbitrary

Synthetic data requirement inadequately analyzed: Table 5D shows catastrophic failure with real data (FID 28.7 vs 13.6) but lacks investigation into why. This constraint deserves deeper study and may limit practical applicability
Time schedule shifting mechanism unexplained: Ablation A shows shifting is important, but intuition for why this works is missing—only empirical validation provided
Missing cascaded diffusion baseline: Cascaded models also progressively increase resolution and are related work, but no direct comparison provided—an important missing baseline
Limited architectural scope: Experiments focus on transformer-based models (DiT). While SDXL (UNet) mentioned, no detailed analysis of architecture robustness or generalization
PDM contribution somewhat incremental: While useful, unclear whether PDM is fundamentally novel or simply another matching loss. Ablation shows it helps, but comparison is limited

strengths: Comprehensive experimental evaluation across multiple architectures (SDXL, SD3.5, FLUX, Wan2.1), datasets, and metrics, with professional human evaluation
Impressive practical speedups (>10× for text-to-image, ~2-3× for text-to-video) while maintaining or improving quality metrics
Insightful latent space spectral analysis (Section 3) providing intuition about frequency characteristics at different noise levels
Thorough ablation studies (Section 5.3) systematically evaluating MMD loss variants and design choices
Strong implementation documentation with extensive appendices enabling reproducibility
Well-presented paper with clear visualizations of method architecture and qualitative results
weaknesses: Limited technical novelty: primarily combines existing techniques (progressive generation, MMD distillation) without introducing fundamentally new concepts or theory
Weak connection between spectral analysis (Section 3) and main method justification; analysis acknowledged to only provide 'averaged results' and schedules remain 'hyperparameters'
Insufficient explanation of why scale-wise distillation works better than alternatives; lacks theoretical justification or mechanistic understanding
Design choices lack principled grounding: scale schedules determined empirically with high variability across models (Appendix C) and no sensitivity analysis provided
Incomplete baseline comparisons: missing recent efficient diffusion methods for text-to-image and other efficient video generation approaches for text-to-video
Limited human evaluation scale: only 2 images per prompt with small total evaluation set, constraining statistical power
Table 6 ablation shows L_MMD-only models remain effective, but paper doesn't establish when MMD is actually necessary versus simpler losses
No analysis of failure cases or prompt types where scale-wise distillation underperforms
Training on synthetic teacher-generated data rather than validating on real prompt distributions; impact on real-world performance unclear
Missing code availability statement and reproducibility gaps regarding exact dataset versions
